definitions.explanation: A place of confinement for prisoners. Has a somewhat literary or historical flavor compared to the more modern {刑務所|けいむしょ}. Often evokes images of traditional or historical prisons with bars and dungeons.

examples.japanese: {罪人|ざいにん}は{牢|ろう}に{入|い}れられた。
examples.english: The criminal was thrown into prison.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{十年間|じゅうねんかん}{牢|ろう}の{中|なか}で{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: He spent ten years in prison.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{主人公|しゅじんこう}は{無実|むじつ}の{罪|つみ}で{牢|ろう}に{入|い}れられたが、{仲間|なかま}の{助|たす}けで{脱獄|だつごく}に{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: The novel's protagonist was imprisoned on a false charge but succeeded in escaping with the help of his companions.

notes:
USAGE:
More literary and evocative than {刑務所|けいむしょ} (prison, penitentiary) or {留置場|りゅうちじょう} (detention center). Frequently appears in historical fiction, fantasy, and dramatic contexts. In everyday conversation about the modern justice system, {刑務所|けいむしょ} is preferred.

COMPOUNDS:
- {牢屋|ろうや}: prison, jail cell (more colloquial)
- {牢獄|ろうごく}: prison, dungeon (literary)
- {入牢|にゅうろう}: imprisonment (historical)
- {脱牢|だつろう}: prison break (historical)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牢|ろう}に{入|い}れる: put in prison
- {牢|ろう}から{出|で}る: get out of prison
- {牢|ろう}の{中|なか}: inside the prison
